CVE only affects deprecated libresolv diagnostic helpers ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, and fp_nquery (deprecated since glibc 2.34). GNU libc GLIBC-SA-2026-0012 states they are for application debugging only and not on the code path executed by the DNS resolver when performing normal lookups. Exposure requires linking code that explicitly calls those helpers when printing crafted DNS RR data while standard workloads use resolver APIs such as getaddrinfo/gethostbyname and do not reach this code.

CVE only affects deprecated libresolv diagnostic helpers ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, and fp_nquery (deprecated since glibc 2.34). GNU libc GLIBC-SA-2026-0011 states they are debugging-only helpers and not on the code path exercised by normal DNS resolver operation. Exposure requires linking code that explicitly calls those entry points while handling arbitrary DNS payloads; resolver usage through standard POSIX/NSS resolver interfaces does not reach this code.

The QMP guest_exec command injection lives in the qemu-system monitor protocol. cdi-importer does not include qemu-system, does not start a QMP listener, and never invokes guest_exec; only qemu-utils binaries (qemu-img, qemu-nbd) are present and none expose QMP.

The QMP migrate command injection lives in the qemu-system monitor protocol. cdi-importer does not include qemu-system, does not start a QMP listener, and does not run VM migrations; only qemu-utils binaries (qemu-img, qemu-nbd) are invoked, none of which expose QMP.

The integer overflow is in the QEMU Guest Agent (qga) command handlers. cdi-importer does not install qemu-guest-agent and never runs inside a guest VM; only qemu-utils is present. The qga code path is not reachable.

The flaw is in the QEMU rocker virtual switch device, exposed only by qemu-system when emulating that hardware for a guest VM. cdi-importer ships qemu-utils only (qemu-img, qemu-nbd, qemu-storage-daemon, qemu-io) for disk image conversion; it does not include or invoke any qemu-system binary, so the rocker code path is not present at runtime.

For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
